name: Discus (Symphysodon aequifasciatus)
description: The king of freshwater aquariums. Discus are prized for their vibrant colors and graceful disc-shaped bodies. They require warm, soft, acidic water conditions and thrive in groups of 6 or more. Feed a varied diet of high-quality flakes, frozen bloodworms, and beef heart.

name: Cardinal Tetra (Paracheirodon axelrodi)
description: Stunning schooling fish with brilliant blue and red coloration that extends the full length of the body. Cardinals are hardier than neon tetras and make excellent community fish. Keep in schools of 10+ for best effect.

name: Cherry Shrimp (Neocaridina davidi)
description: Popular dwarf shrimp prized for their bright red coloration and algae-eating abilities. Easy to breed and incredibly active, cherry shrimp are perfect for nano tanks and planted aquariums. They thrive in stable water parameters with plenty of hiding spots.

name: Betta Splendens (Siamese Fighting Fish)
description: Magnificent labyrinth fish known for their flowing fins and vibrant colors. Males must be kept alone, but females can be kept in sororities. Bettas appreciate planted tanks with gentle filtration and warm water around 26-28°C.

name: Ocellaris Clownfish (Amphiprion ocellaris)
description: The iconic orange clownfish, made famous by Finding Nemo. Hardy and personable, they are the perfect starter saltwater fish. They will readily host anemones or simply claim a favorite corner of the tank. Best kept in pairs.

name: Java Fern (Microsorum pteropus)
description: One of the most undemanding aquarium plants available. Java fern grows attached to driftwood or rocks (never bury the rhizome). Thrives in low light and all water conditions. Perfect for beginners and low-tech tanks.

name: Monte Carlo (Micranthemum tweediei)
description: Popular foreground carpeting plant that creates a lush green lawn when grown correctly. Requires moderate to high light and CO2 injection for best results. Can be grown emersed or submerged.

name: Bucephalandra 'Wavy Green'
description: Slow-growing epiphyte with beautiful textured leaves that range from bright green to deep blue under high light. Like Java fern, attach to hardscape rather than planting in substrate. Extremely hardy and adaptable.

name: Corydoras paleatus (Peppered Cory)
description: Adorable bottom-dwelling catfish with a charming personality. Keep in groups of 4+ on a soft sand substrate to protect their delicate barbels. They are active during the day and will entertain you with their antics.

name: Red Root Floater (Phyllanthus fluitans)
description: Beautiful floating plant with small round leaves that turn deep red under high light. Long red roots hang down providing cover for fry and shrimp. Excellent for nutrient export and creating shaded areas in the aquarium.
